paper.title_en: Novel observables for exploring jet quenching effects in individual jets
paper.abstract_en: We introduce event-shape observables in the jet frame to characterize intra-jet shapes and study medium modifications in heavy-ion collisions. Using the JEWEL model, we investigate jet constituent angular and transverse momentum distributions, together with two representative event-shape observables, transverse thrust $τ_\perp$ and transverse sphericity $S_\perp$, in $p$+$p$ and 0--10% central Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.02\,\mathrm{TeV}$. These observables are evaluated after transforming the jet constituent momenta into the jet frame. The intra-jet shape distributions in Pb+Pb collisions shift toward larger values relative to those in $p$+$p$ collisions, indicating more isotropic distributions of constituent transverse momenta. Comparisons between calculations with and without recoil, along with the dependence on the constituent transverse momentum threshold, indicate that medium response plays an important role in these modifications. These results suggest that jet-frame event-shape observables provide sensitive probes of medium response in jet quenching, complementary to single-particle angular and transverse momentum distributions.
